\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تهمة} (tuhma)}{تهمة (tuhma)}]{\ar{تهمة} (tuhma) — an accusation, a charge}

\label{lesson:AR-C348-tuhma}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a ransom, then the Arabic for a kidnapper.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تهمة}}
\textbf{\ar{تهمة}} — \emph{tuhma} — \textquotedblleft{}an accusation, a charge\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كانت} \ar{التهمة} \ar{سرقة} \ar{سيارة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kānat at-tuhma sariqat sayyāra.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The charge was stealing a car.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ar{تهم}, \emph{tuham}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تهمة}} (\emph{tuhma}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{w-h-m} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to fancy, to suspect\textquotedblright{}. In \emph{tuhma} the \emph{w} of the root shows as \emph{t}, as in \emph{ittahama}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tuhma}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tuhma}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kānat at-tuhma sariqat sayyāra.} — The charge was stealing a car.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a ransom, then the Arabic for a kidnapper, then say \emph{tuhma} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{تهمة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An accusation, a charge\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{جناية} (jināya)}{جناية (jināya)}]{\ar{جناية} (jināya) — a felony, a serious crime}

\label{lesson:AR-C348-jinaya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a kidnapper, then the Arabic for an accusation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{جناية}}
\textbf{\ar{جناية}} — \emph{jināya} — \textquotedblleft{}a felony, a serious crime\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كانت} \ar{السرقة} \ar{بالسلاح} \ar{جناية}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kānat as-sariqa bi-s-silāḥ jināya.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The armed robbery was a felony.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{جناية}} (\emph{jināya}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{j-n-y} (Lane), where \emph{janā} is \textquotedblleft{}to gather fruit\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{janā ʿalā} \textquotedblleft{}to commit an offence against someone\textquotedblright{}: to reap harm for him.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jināya}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jināya}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kānat as-sariqa bi-s-silāḥ jināya.} — The armed robbery was a felony.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a kidnapper, then the Arabic for an accusation, then say \emph{jināya} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{جناية} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A felony, a serious crime\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{عقوبة} (ʿuqūba)}{عقوبة (ʿuqūba)}]{\ar{عقوبة} (ʿuqūba) — a penalty, a punishment}

\label{lesson:AR-C348-uquba}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for an accusation, then the Arabic for a felony.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{عقوبة}}
\textbf{\ar{عقوبة}} — \emph{ʿuqūba} — \textquotedblleft{}a penalty, a punishment\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كانت} \ar{العقوبة} \ar{سنة} \ar{في} \ar{السجن}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kānat al-ʿuqūba sana fī as-sijn.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The penalty was a year in prison.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{عقوبة}} (\emph{ʿuqūba}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-q-b} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to come after, to follow at the heel\textquotedblright{}. A punishment is what comes after the deed.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿuqūba}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿuqūba}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kānat al-ʿuqūba sana fī as-sijn.} — The penalty was a year in prison.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for an accusation, then the Arabic for a felony, then say \emph{ʿuqūba} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{عقوبة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A penalty, a punishment\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{عاقب} (ʿāqaba)}{عاقب (ʿāqaba)}]{\ar{عاقب} (ʿāqaba) — to punish}

\label{lesson:AR-C348-aqaba}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a felony, then the Arabic for a penalty.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{عاقب}}
\textbf{\ar{عاقب}} — \emph{ʿāqaba} — \textquotedblleft{}to punish\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{عاقب} \ar{المعلم} \ar{الطالب} \ar{على} \ar{كذبه}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ʿāqaba al-muʿallim aṭ-ṭālib ʿalā kadhibihi.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The teacher punished the pupil for lying.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يعاقب}, \emph{yuʿāqib}.

It takes \ar{على} for the deed.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{عاقب}} (\emph{ʿāqaba}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-q-b} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to follow after\textquotedblright{}. It is Form III, \textquotedblleft{}to requite someone for what he did\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿāqaba}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿāqaba}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿāqaba al-muʿallim aṭ-ṭālib ʿalā kadhibihi.} — The teacher punished the pupil for lying.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a felony, then the Arabic for a penalty, then say \emph{ʿāqaba} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{عاقب} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To punish\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{بلغ} (ballagha)}{بلغ (ballagha)}]{\ar{بلغ} (ballagha) — to inform the police; to report}

\label{lesson:AR-C348-ballagha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a penalty, then the Arabic for to punish.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{بلغ}}
\textbf{\ar{بلغ}} — \emph{ballagha} — \textquotedblleft{}to inform the police; to report\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{بلغ} \ar{الجار} \ar{الشرطة} \ar{عن} \ar{الصوت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ballagha al-jār ash-shurṭa ʿan aṣ-ṣawt.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The neighbour told the police about the noise.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يبلغ}, \emph{yuballigh}.

\ar{بلغ} \ar{عن}: to report something. The plain verb, \emph{balagha}, is to reach.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{بلغ}} (\emph{ballagha}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{b-l-gh} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to reach\textquotedblright{}. It is Form II, \textquotedblleft{}to make news reach someone\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ballagha}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ballagha}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ballagha al-jār ash-shurṭa ʿan aṣ-ṣawt.} — The neighbour told the police about the noise.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a penalty, then the Arabic for to punish, then say \emph{ballagha} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{بلغ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To inform the police; to report\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[(dialogue)]{Words from chapters 341–348 — a review}

\label{lesson:AR-R348-review-341-348}



\begin{quote}
Say the Arabic for a knight and a helmet.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a knight, a helmet, a truce, a treaty, to betray
  \item heritage, a manuscript, an inscription, a title, to invent
  \item an adventure, unknown, a surprise, a coincidence, to take a risk
  \item a woodcutter, to enchant, to turn into, to come true, to take revenge
  \item to challenge, to confront, to overcome, to approach, to move away
  \item to spy, to disguise oneself, to suspect, to sneak in, to chase
  \item to kidnap, to catch up with, a hostage, a ransom, a kidnapper
  \item an accusation, a felony, a penalty, to punish, to inform the police
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A knight? (\textbf{\ar{فارس}}, \emph{fāris}.) A helmet? (\textbf{\ar{خوذة}}, \emph{khūdha}.) A truce? (\textbf{\ar{هدنة}}, \emph{hudna}.) A treaty? (\textbf{\ar{معاهدة}}, \emph{muʿāhada}.) To betray? (\textbf{\ar{خان}}, \emph{khāna}.) Heritage? (\textbf{\ar{تراث}}, \emph{turāth}.) A manuscript? (\textbf{\ar{مخطوطة}}, \emph{makhṭūṭa}.) An inscription? (\textbf{\ar{نقش}}, \emph{naqsh}.) A title? (\textbf{\ar{لقب}}, \emph{laqab}.) To invent? (\textbf{\ar{اخترع}}, \emph{ikhtaraʿa}.) An adventure? (\textbf{\ar{مغامرة}}, \emph{mughāmara}.) Unknown? (\textbf{\ar{مجهول}}, \emph{majhūl}.) A surprise? (\textbf{\ar{مفاجأة}}, \emph{mufājaʾa}.) A coincidence? (\textbf{\ar{صدفة}}, \emph{ṣudfa}.) To take a risk? (\textbf{\ar{خاطر}}, \emph{khāṭara}.) A woodcutter? (\textbf{\ar{حطاب}}, \emph{ḥaṭṭāb}.) To enchant? (\textbf{\ar{سحر}}, \emph{saḥara}.) To turn into? (\textbf{\ar{تحول}}, \emph{taḥawwala}.) To come true? (\textbf{\ar{تحقق}}, \emph{taḥaqqaqa}.) To take revenge? (\textbf{\ar{انتقم}}, \emph{intaqama}.) To challenge? (\textbf{\ar{تحدى}}, \emph{taḥaddā}.) To confront? (\textbf{\ar{واجه}}, \emph{wājaha}.) To overcome? (\textbf{\ar{تغلب}}, \emph{taghallaba}.) To approach? (\textbf{\ar{اقترب}}, \emph{iqtaraba}.) To move away? (\textbf{\ar{ابتعد}}, \emph{ibtaʿada}.) To spy? (\textbf{\ar{تجسس}}, \emph{tajassasa}.) To disguise oneself? (\textbf{\ar{تنكر}}, \emph{tanakkara}.) To suspect? (\textbf{\ar{اشتبه}}, \emph{ishtabaha}.) To sneak in? (\textbf{\ar{تسلل}}, \emph{tasallala}.) To chase? (\textbf{\ar{طارد}}, \emph{ṭārada}.) To kidnap? (\textbf{\ar{اختطف}}, \emph{ikhtaṭafa}.) To catch up with? (\textbf{\ar{لحق}}, \emph{laḥiqa}.) A hostage? (\textbf{\ar{رهينة}}, \emph{rahīna}.) A ransom? (\textbf{\ar{فدية}}, \emph{fidya}.) A kidnapper? (\textbf{\ar{خاطف}}, \emph{khāṭif}.) An accusation? (\textbf{\ar{تهمة}}, \emph{tuhma}.) A felony? (\textbf{\ar{جناية}}, \emph{jināya}.) A penalty? (\textbf{\ar{عقوبة}}, \emph{ʿuqūba}.) To punish? (\textbf{\ar{عاقب}}, \emph{ʿāqaba}.) To inform the police? (\textbf{\ar{بلغ}}, \emph{ballagha}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
